newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY FARMERS GO AHEAD WOTH BORDER PROTEST.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY FARMERS GO AHEAD WOTH BORDER PROTEST.

text.p: A group of Hungarian farmers proceeded with their plan to disrupt border traffic on Wednesday despite the country's Parliament passing tax concessions designed to meet some of their demands.
Hungarian border police said they had not received any specific orders on how to deal with the protest, organised by the militant farmers union METESZ.

"We were warned of their arrival but have received no special instructions " Lieutenant-Colonel Lajos Varga, commander of the Tompa border crossing with Serbia told Reuters. "We will follow the normal checking routine."

METESZ said earlier it planned to slow down traffic on Hungary's roads by blocking one lane and would attempt to hinder the flow of vehicles at frontiers with six neighbouring countries by repeatedly crossing the border with their cars.
Varga said even if the farmers brought hundreds of vehicles as they had planned, his border post would be able to cope as Tompa handles between 6,000 and 20,000 vehicles a day.
"We are more concerned about East European guest workers returning home for the Easter vacation," he said.

Zoltan Timar, deputy spokesman of National Border Guard said the only other border crossing so far affected was Gyula, on the Romanian border, where 30 vehicles had appeared but had decided not to cross the border after consultations with border guards on both sides.
"We dont know what they plan," said Timar. "They will probably move around on the road leading to the frontier, staying on the Hungarian side of the border."
National police spokesman Andras Rozsa told Reuters there had been no violent incidents so far.
"They seem very disciplined and respect the traffic regulations," he said.

Late on Tuesday night, Parliament voted overwhelmingly to inprove taxation and social security payment obligations for agricultural producers but METESZ leaders had said in advance the measures did not go far enough and would not prevent their protest action.

METESZ is one of the smaller but more radical of Hungary's almost 30 farmers' unions which have so far failed to establish a common stance over land ownership, distribution of subsidies and farming taxation.
Other unions have witheld support for the protests in advance of a planned round table conference on the future of Hungary's agriculture.
